question.problem:
Which of the following statements are true?

I. Any $4\times 2$ matrix $A$ has at most $2$ distinct singular values.

II. Any matrix of the form  $A=[\begin{aligned}-a & 0 \\ 0 & a\end{aligned}]$ has exactly one negative and one positive singular value.

III. Any $2\times 4$ matrix $A$ has at most $4$ distinct singular values.
question.worked_solution:
The singular values of the matrix $A$ are the square roots of the eigenvalues of the matrix ${A}^{T}\,A.$ 

With that in mind, let's examine our statements.

- Statement I is true. Since $A$ is a $4\times 2$ matrix and ${A}^{T}$ is a $2\times 4$ matrix, ${A}^{T}\,A$ must be a $2\times 2$ matrix: 

$$
{{A}^{T}}_{2\times 4}\times {A}_{4\times 2}={{A}^{T}\,A}_{2\times 2}
$$

Hence, $A$ has at most $2$ distinct singular values.

- Statement II is false.  All singular values of any matrix are non-negative. So, 
$A$  can't have any negative singular value.

- Statement III is true.  Indeed,  since $A$ is a $2\times 4$ matrix and ${A}^{T}$ is a $4\times 2$ matrix, ${A}^{T}\,A$ must be a $4\times 4$ matrix: 

$$
{{A}^{T}}_{4\times 2}\times {A}_{2\times 4}={{A}^{T}\,A}_{4\times 4}
$$

Hence, $A$ has at most $4$ distinct singular values.

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and III only."
